    The whole trip in one minute

    Our two-day timeline

    Tap a stop. All times are Singapore time (SGT), taken from the posts and from when each video file was built.

    Stop 1 · The spark

    Karpathy's funnel: how the world uses AI

    On 12 Oct 2026 at 3:12 AM SGT, Andrej Karpathy posted on X that the gap in how people understand AI is widening. It is "less two groups of people speaking past each other and more a sharp funnel." He sketched four tiers with "napkin math".

    ~6 billion · barely touched AI (~75%)
    1 to 2 billion · casual free chatbot users (~20%)
    ~20 million · frontier AI for maths and code (0.2%)
    ~5,000 · inside the labs

    Flip each card to see what Karpathy actually wrote. The front shows how our kids say it.

    What drives the funnel? (his three reasons)

    1. Ambition, problem size and horizon. "A question with a paragraph answer barely stresses the system. You need a reservoir of big, difficult problems that you really care about."
    2. Jaggedness. AI is strongest in work that is "digital, verifiable and economically valuable", like maths and code.
    3. Access. "Free-tier, paid-tier, internal."

    "So this is the weirdness of the moment... And it is all happening at the same time."

    Creativity move: find the human picture inside the idea. Karpathy wrote about percentages. We asked: what would four kids standing side by side say if each one lived in a different tier? Same street, same day, four worlds.
    Stop 2 · The inspiration

    Riley Brown's "visual reading"

    About four hours after Karpathy, at 7:18 AM SGT on 12 Oct, Riley Brown quoted the post with a video and these words:

    "Here's Opus 5.5 with a visual reading of Karpathy's latest tweet. Watch on 2x speed. (one prompt btw)"

    What the video shows (we checked its frames and its audio):

    • A tall, phone-shaped video, 3 minutes 44 seconds long.
    • A voice reads Karpathy's post aloud, from "Napkin math, somewhere around 6 billion people" to "And it is all happening at the same time."
    • A hand-drawn funnel fills in tier by tier on off-white paper while a pencil sketches: 6B (about 75%), 1 to 2B (about 20%), 20M (0.2%) and 5,000 (0.00006%), with small doodles such as chat bubbles, a keyboard and code editor, and a stack labelled 722 for the maths manuscripts.
    • Bold captions run word by word along the bottom, with key words highlighted in yellow.
    • It then draws the three drivers (ambition, jaggedness, access) and ends on the whole funnel as one picture.

    Read on 14 Oct 2026 (SGT) through the X API: about 158,000 views and 2,036 likes. Frames shown small, with credit, to describe the video. All rights stay with the creator.

    Riley's version

    Explains the whole post. One narrator, one drawing, about 4 minutes (2 at 2x).

    Our remix

    Shows the gap. Four kids, four lines, one number each, about 22 to 28 seconds. Then the same idea in new styles, cities and languages.
    Creativity move: borrow the form, change the audience. Riley proved one prompt can turn a dense post into a video. We kept the source facts and changed who it is for: kids, families and teachers.
    Stop 3 · The original styles

    Six ways to tell the same story

    Before picking one look, we tried six. Rule for all of them: "inspired by" a style only, with no real logos, brands, characters or artists. Tap a style.

    Innovation move: go wide before you go deep. Six quick styles on the first night let King compare them side by side. The cartoon town look became the base for every city version.
    Stop 4 · Scripting

    Four kids, four lines, four numbers

    Tap a kid. Each one speaks once, and a paper tag with one number pops up at the bottom of the screen.

    Script v1 or final? Flip the switch

      Creativity move: one line, one number, one laugh. Each kid line is a tiny joke a child could say. The tag carries the fact. Words never pile more than one idea on screen at once.

        🌺 Little India: the final video

        How we tested the language with AI

        Dated 14 Oct 2026. Nobody on the team speaks Tamil, so we checked it in layers. Each layer catches different problems.

        1. Speech to text, several times. We ran the transcript checker on the takes again and again to see which word the kid actually says: "check" (செக்) or "செய்து" (doing). On the chosen take, 8 of 10 runs heard "check".
        2. Text reviews. Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6-Astra (high reasoning) reviewed the script and transcripts. They read text only, so they cannot hear the voice. Their review led to an earlier fix: the line 4 ending was retaken so it says "checking it", not "doing it", and the tag wording was corrected.
        3. An audio review. Gemini (Google's model, which can take the audio in) listened to the final video. It said lines 1 to 3 are correct and natural. It said line 4 is understandable but awkward: "பத்து வருஷம் எடுக்கற" is a calque, a word for word copy of the English "takes 10 years" (native would be "ஆகுற" or "பிடிக்கிற"), the subject and verb don't match in number (plural agents, so "முடிச்சிருக்காங்க"), and the pacing is rushed with an abrupt ending.
        AI checks catch a lot. But before publishing, a native Tamil speaker still needs to listen and judge natural pronunciation, tone and phrasing.
        Innovation move: localise the world, not just the words. Mandarin kids say "a fancy Baidu", not "a fancy Google". The Hong Kong lines mix in English words like "app" and "check", as people there often do. Models can read text but can't hear tones, so a person still listens to every line.

        The toolbox

        What we used, with versions

        Make your own in seven steps

        Find a spark

        A post with a surprising number or a clear picture. Ours: Karpathy's funnel.

        Borrow a form

        See how someone else told it (Riley's drawing), then change the audience.

        Go wide

        Try several styles fast. Keep the one people want to share.

        Write tiny lines

        One speaker, one line, one number. Facts on tags, jokes in mouths.

        Make the still

        Wide shot, kids well spaced, faces clear of the bottom strip.

        Clip, cut, check

        One clip per kid. Check first frames, transcripts and pitch. Then a human listens.

        Localise

        New street, landmarks and language. Ask a native speaker before you ship.
